title: network_state.json
description: External-attacker view of one or more targets, produced by network-prober/ and consumed by exposure-analyzer/. See docs/DESIGN.md §1.4.2 for the contract rationale. Flat per-(target,port) list, JSONL-friendly for large scans (each element is a self-contained record).

target.description: The hostname or IP the prober was invoked against, as-given (no reverse-DNS rewriting). E.g. 'db-exposed' inside the eval compose network, 'server.example.com' or '10.0.0.42' in production.

reachable.description: True iff the prober received a response consistent with an open port (TCP handshake completed, UDP got an application-level reply). 'filtered' / 'closed' / 'no reply' all map to false; the distinction is not preserved because the analyzer does not need it.

banner.description: Raw fingerprint string as returned by the prober (nmap -sV service line, TLS server-hello product, or a stripped protocol-level banner). Preserved verbatim so the analyzer prompt can reason about it even when service_guess is absent. Absent iff reachable is false or the prober got no banner.

service_guess.description: Parsed by the banner-parser table. Absent when the banner is missing or the parser has no rule for it. The raw 'banner' field is the fallback in that case.
